newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Emetel says its assets worth $2.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Emetel says its assets worth $2.4 bln.

text.p: The head of Ecuador's telephone company Emetel said Thursday that bidders for the company, which is due to be privatized, should assume its assets are worth about $2.4 billion.

Emetel President Manuel Zhindon told journalists the valuation had been carried out by the international consortium Gerasin. But the executive said the $2.4 billion figure "is nothing more than a reference point."
Ecuador's government on Tuesday extended the bidding period in the international tender for the 35 percent stake of Emetel for the second time to November 29 from October 30.
Some 19 European, U.S. and Asian firms have expressed interest in the company including Bell Atlantic Corp, British Telecom and France Telecom.
